Notes: Jewish population; source says Jews began to settle at the beginning of the 19th century
Under the 1823 Regulation of the Kingdom of Poland Jews were allowed to live in certain parts of the city (presence documented; no count)
Old Jewish cemetery founded on ul. Nowomiejska (organized community presence; no count)
Kahal functioned by 1842 or earlier when 791 Jews lived there
Approx. 13500 out of general population of 60000 at outbreak of WWII; community swelled by refugees from neighbouring communities

3000 remaining Jews segregated into ghetto (October 1940) after earlier deportations; ghetto liquidated 27 April 1942 with all inmates sent to Chelmno (death toll/transit not used as population) [Review fix: Population 3000 moved to Notes - ghetto count (people remaining after earlier deportations), not the town's population]
Surviving remnants gradually returned after the war; Wikipedia says nearly 1000 Jews returned (returnee count, year approximate, not a resident census)
By the late 1960s the community had disappeared (most left for Israel; last after Six-Day War 1967); year approximate
